$comment: 收据:本仓库哪些数字可复现、哪些明确不可复现。核对于 2026-09-14。规则:凡对外宣称的量化结论,要么在这里给出可跑的命令,要么明确标注不可复现——不允许既不标来源也不标不可复现。每条 claim 的 check 由 .github/workflows/claims.yml 每周跑一次。

claims.claim: The test suite passes on a clean checkout.
claims.method: node --test over the repo's test files (package.json scripts.test -> scripts/run-tests.js).

claims.claim: Lint is a hard gate: ESLint runs with --max-warnings=0, so a single warning fails.
claims.method: package.json scripts.lint is exactly 'eslint . --max-warnings=0'; scripts.check runs lint then test.

claims.claim: The Agent-vs-Legacy benchmark table (20.5s / 10.1s / 100% success, one private group, 56 days, 5 questions), the 93% check-in-bot share of @me hits, and the 3011ms → 1407ms figure for the 2×429 retry recovery in the same warning paragraph — in README.md / README.zh-CN.md / docs/agent-qa.md — are directional historical records and are NOT reproducible.
claims.metric: the published figures as stated: the benchmark table's summary rows, plus the 93% noise share, which is restated 2× in README.md, 2× in README.zh-CN.md and 1× in docs/agent-qa.md
claims.method: All three documents label the table stale; the 93% share is published as 实测/measured with no committed harness or dataset behind it. No figure in that family is asserted as current, in either language.
claims.repro: grep -c '已过期且不可复现' docs/agent-qa.md README.zh-CN.md; grep -c 'stale and not reproducible' README.md; grep -c '93%' README.md README.zh-CN.md docs/agent-qa.md
claims.evidence: docs/agent-qa.md#benchmark-结果; README.md (AI Features → Benchmark); README.zh-CN.md (AI 功能 → Benchmark)

check.manual: no committed artifact recomputes any of these: the harness that produced 20.5s / 10.1s / 100% lived in eval/, an agent scratch directory untracked in ee2a63d (git ls-files eval/ is empty and the directory is gone from the tree), and it ran against a private Weibo group archive (one group, 56 days, 5 questions — not in the repo). The 93% share is the same shape of number: a measured proportion (the check-in bot's share of @me hits) with no committed dataset or script behind it, now restated in three documents (README.md ×2, README.zh-CN.md ×2, docs/agent-qa.md ×1), so it belongs to this entry instead of a second one. The 2×429 recovery figure in the same warning paragraph (3011ms → 1407ms) is likewise a live-API measurement made during the pi-agent-core migration, not a repository fact. All of it predates the block-level BM25 retrieval rewrite and the pi-agent-core loop migration, so re-running anything today would measure different code — that is why README.md, README.zh-CN.md and docs/agent-qa.md all label the table stale, and why current numbers must come from scripts/benchmark-qa.js instead.

claims.claim: Current latency numbers can be produced locally by the shipped script instead of being quoted from the stale table.
claims.metric: script exists and carries the 4 documented flags
claims.method: docs/agent-qa.md documents --group / --repeat / --questions / --json; README points at it for current numbers.

claims.claim: Sending an image from the group input box is capped at 20MB (README.md “up to 20MB”; README.zh-CN.md “上限 20MB”).
claims.metric: MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024, enforced by sendGroupImage before it uploads anything
claims.method: lib/send-message.js compares the buffer against the cap and refuses with the cap in the message; the check feeds 21MiB (must be refused) and exactly 20MiB (must pass the gate) through a stubbed fetch, so no network is touched.
claims.repro: node -e "const s=require('./lib/send-message.js');const stub=async()=>({json:async()=>({error_code:21301})});(async()=>{const over=await s.sendGroupImage({groupId:'1',buffer:Buffer.alloc(21*1024*1024),fetchImpl:stub});const at=await s.sendGroupImage({groupId:'1',buffer:Buffer.alloc(20*1024*1024),fetchImpl:stub});console.log((over.ok===false&&over.error.includes('20MB')?'21.0MB refused (>20MB)':'UNEXPECTED: '+JSON.stringify(over))+' · '+(at.needLogin===true?'20.0MB accepted':'NOT ACCEPTED: '+JSON.stringify(at)))})()"

check.cmd: node -e "const s=require('./lib/send-message.js');const stub=async()=>({json:async()=>({error_code:21301})});(async()=>{const over=await s.sendGroupImage({groupId:'1',buffer:Buffer.alloc(21*1024*1024),fetchImpl:stub});const at=await s.sendGroupImage({groupId:'1',buffer:Buffer.alloc(20*1024*1024),fetchImpl:stub});console.log((over.ok===false&&over.error.includes('20MB')?'21.0MB refused (>20MB)':'UNEXPECTED: '+JSON.stringify(over))+' · '+(at.needLogin===true?'20.0MB accepted':'NOT ACCEPTED: '+JSON.stringify(at)))})()"

claims.claim: The emoticon picker and the tag renderer reuse Weibo's official 340-entry emoticon list (README.md “the 340-entry official list”; README.zh-CN.md “340 条官方清单”).
claims.metric: entries of Weibo's official list (https://api.weibo.com/webim/emotions.json) that lib/emotions.js accepts
claims.method: lib/emotions.js commits no list: it fetches the official JSON at runtime (SOURCE_URL) and keeps the entries whose phrase is [label] with an http(s) url. The 340 figure is restated in prose only (lib/emotions.js header comment, lib/text-utils.js JSDoc) and in both READMEs — nothing committed contains the entries themselves.
claims.repro: curl -s 'https://api.weibo.com/webim/emotions.json?source=209678993' | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>console.log(Object.keys(require('./lib/emotions.js').toPhraseMap(JSON.parse(d))).length))"   # needs a logged-in Weibo cookie

check.manual: 340 cannot be recomputed inside the repository: no committed copy of the list exists, lib/emotions.js only knows its URL, and the runtime cache (cache/emotions.json) is gitignored. The endpoint is not readable without a Weibo session either — an unauthenticated GET returns {"error_code":21301,"error":"auth by Null spi!"} — so a weekly gate could not fetch it even with network access. What would make this checkable: a committed snapshot of that JSON (or of the cache file) with the entry count asserted against it, plus its own date, since Weibo keeps adding emoticons and the count is a moving target.

claims.claim: The Tauri sidecar is a ~60MB standalone binary (README.md / README.zh-CN.md, desktop architecture).
claims.metric: size of the binary sidecar/build.mjs writes to src-tauri/binaries/viewer-server-<target-triple>
claims.method: sidecar/build.mjs runs `bun build scripts/viewer-server.js --compile` and prints the result as (bytes/1024/1024).toFixed(1) MB. Both destinations it writes to (sidecar/dist/, src-tauri/binaries/) are gitignored, so no built artifact is committed to measure.
claims.repro: node sidecar/build.mjs   # prints "[sidecar] Size: NN.N MB"

check.manual: the number is an output of an artifact-producing build, not a read of committed data: src-tauri/binaries/ and sidecar/dist/ are in .gitignore and no binary is in the tree. Reproducing it means running `bun build --compile` over scripts/viewer-server.js (with the npm dependencies installed) plus `rustc --print host-tuple`, in a gate that has neither bun nor Rust installed — and the result would track the pinned Bun version and dependency tree rather than the commit, so a freshly built size would drift from the sentence without anything having gone wrong. What would make it checkable: a committed size manifest, or a CI step that builds the sidecar and compares the printed size.

claims.claim: Every page in this repository that animates — through CSS animations or transitions, cross-document view transitions, SMIL, requestAnimationFrame or the Web Animations API — also handles prefers-reduced-motion, so a reader who asked their system for less motion gets none.
claims.value: every animated page carries the reduced-motion branch
claims.metric: HTML pages containing a motion primitive vs those containing prefers-reduced-motion
claims.method: The detector enumerates ways a page can move (animation:, @keyframes, <animate, requestAnimationFrame, .animate(, transition:, @view-transition); a page matching any of them must also contain prefers-reduced-motion. It also asserts that at least one page matched, so it cannot pass vacuously on a tree with no animation at all.
claims.repro: python3 -c "import re,pathlib;m=re.compile(r'transition\s*:|@keyframes');print([str(p) for p in pathlib.Path('.').rglob('*.html') if m.search(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8',errors='replace'))])"

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
skip = {'.git','node_modules','dist','build','coverage'}
moves = re.compile(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes|<animate\b|requestAnimationFrame|\.animate\(|transition\s*:|@view-transition')
files = [p for p in sorted(pathlib.Path('.').rglob('*.html')) if not (set(p.parts) & skip)]
animated = [p for p in files if moves.search(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))]
missing = [str(p) for p in animated if 'prefers-reduced-motion' not in p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')]
assert animated, 'no animated page found: this receipt would pass vacuously'
assert not missing, missing
print('files %d animated %d missing %s' % (len(files), len(animated), missing))"
